rail.label: Screens
info.target: Another broker is any broker you reach over the network. This app's broker is the one built into MQTT Panel: choosing it fills host, port, transport and certificates from its running setup. You can still edit them.
info.verifyServer: The client checks that the broker presents a certificate signed by a CA it trusts. Protects against connecting to an impostor.
info.caCert: The certificate of the authority that signed the broker's certificate. Needed when the broker uses a private or self-signed certificate; leave empty for brokers with a public certificate.
info.clientCert: Identifies this computer to the broker, instead of or in addition to a password. Only needed if the broker requires client certificates (mutual TLS).
info.clientKey: The private key belonging to the client certificate. Stored in the OS keychain, never in the profile file.
info.sni: The host name sent to the broker during the TLS handshake. Leave empty to use the host above; only change it if the broker serves several names on one address.
info.alpn: Tells the broker which protocol is wanted over TLS. Some cloud brokers require a specific value (for example mqtt); leave empty otherwise.
info.filters: Filters decide which topics this connection receives. # means everything; building/+/temperature means one level of wildcard.

info.request: Request and response is an MQTT 5 feature. Your message carries a response topic and a correlation ID. The device answers on that response topic and copies the correlation ID into its reply. MQTT Panel subscribes to the response topic for you, matches the reply by correlation ID and shows it next to the sent entry. Broker and device must both speak MQTT 5; on 3.1.1 this section is not available.

info.anonymous: When on, anyone who can reach a listener can connect without a password or certificate. Users, per-listener logins and client certificates are kept but not checked until you turn it off. Use it only on a network you trust.
info.requireClientCert: Require client certificate: the broker only accepts clients that present a certificate issued by the CA above. Replaces passwords with something that cannot be guessed.
info.reachable: Network: any device that can reach this computer can connect to this listener, subject to the authentication below. Localhost: only programs on this computer can connect.
info.login: One optional username and password for this listener, accepted in addition to the shared users list. Stored in the system keychain. On a Mutual TLS listener the client certificate stays required.
info.preset.plain: No encryption and no login: anyone who reaches the port can read and send messages. Enough on a lab bench or a network you fully control, never on a building or site network.
info.preset.encrypted: Traffic is encrypted and clients can check that they talk to this broker (with CA.pem). Protects against eavesdropping and impostor brokers, but anyone who reaches the port can still connect.
info.preset.passwords: Encrypted, and every client needs a username and password. Protects against eavesdropping and strangers; a leaked password has to be changed here.
info.preset.mtls: Encrypted, and every device needs its own client certificate issued here. The strongest setup: nothing to guess, and one device can be revoked without touching the others.
info.certName: The device name or its client ID. It becomes the certificate's common name (CN), which the broker log shows when the device connects.
info.passphrase: Protects only the exported file (the PKCS#12 bundle or the PEM key). It is not the broker login and not a listener password. The device asks for it once, when the certificate is installed.
preset.plain.short: No encryption, anyone can connect. For a trusted lab network only.
preset.encrypted.short: Clients verify the broker. Uses the local CA and server certificate.
preset.passwords.short: Encrypted, and each client needs a username and password.
preset.mtls.short: Encrypted, and each device needs its own client certificate, issued on the Broker screen. No passwords.
preset.plain.what: Messages travel unencrypted and nobody has to prove who they are. Use it on a lab bench only. It will add a TCP listener without encryption; the other listeners are not changed.
preset.encrypted.what: The broker proves who it is with its server certificate, signed by the local CA. Install CA.pem on devices so they can check it. Anyone who reaches the port can connect. It will add a TLS listener with the local CA and server certificate; the other listeners are not changed.
preset.passwords.what: Like Encrypted, and every client logs in with a username and password from the users list or this listener's own login. It will add a TLS listener that requires a login; the other listeners are not changed.
preset.mtls.what: The broker proves who it is with its server certificate, and each device proves who it is with a client certificate you issue. Install CA.pem on the device together with its certificate. This is the strongest setup and needs no passwords. It will turn on "require client certificate" for this listener and use the local CA; the other listeners are not changed.
